stage

normal acinus PanIN / tumour epithelium collagen / ECM CAF / stellate cell T cell vessel lumen

Hover or focus a part for a short explanation. Drag the slider to the right: a low-grade PanIN among normal acini becomes high-grade, then invasive PDA; the acini are mostly replaced, collagen builds around CAFs, the vessel collapses and T cells are held out of the stroma.

Sources

Educational only, not medical advice. Schematic histology-style section of PanIN progressing to invasive PDA, not to scale and not a measured section; cell counts and levels come from a qualitative model. Not purely tumour-promoting: in mice, deleting alpha-SMA+ myofibroblasts or the stroma made tumours more aggressive (Özdemir 2014; Rhim 2014). Data from mouse models (Olive 2009, Provenzano 2012, Jacobetz 2013, Clark 2007) are marked mouse in the hover text. A schematic of human PDA stroma; where the evidence is from mouse models or cell culture, the hover text says so. No measured value is drawn: the slider, the cell counts and every level are qualitative, and no stromal percentage is shown (the sources say the stroma is the majority of the tumour mass, not by how much).

  • Stroma, cell types, immunosuppression. Kleeff J et al., Pancreatic cancer, Nat Rev Dis Primers 2016;2:16022 (PMID 27158978, doi:10.1038/nrdp.2016.22): abundant dense collagenous stroma; CAFs make the collagen and arise from several sources, activated stellate cells among them; immune infiltrate suppressive. Neesse A et al., Stromal biology and therapy in pancreatic cancer, Gut 2019;68:159-171 (PMID 30177543, doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2018-316451): TME components (CAFs, immune cells, matrix, vessels, nerves).
  • Pathology. Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 9th ed. (Kumar, Abbas, Aster), ch.19 The Pancreas, p.909 of the PDF: poorly formed malignant glands of pleomorphic cuboidal to columnar cells in an intense desmoplastic reaction; perineural, lymphatic and large-vessel invasion. Beger et al., The Pancreas, 4th ed., Wiley 2023, ch.125 (Pittman, Hruban), ch.123 (CAFs and macrophages, immunosuppression) and ch.9 (Apte et al., stellate cells 4-7% of parenchymal cells). These are the project's vetted notes (docs/book-notes/).
  • CAFs and stellate cells (stellate cells are one of several CAF sources). Apte MV et al., Periacinar stellate shaped cells in rat pancreas, Gut 1998;43:128-33 (PMID 9771417, doi:10.1136/gut.43.1.128): periacinar, lipid-droplet (vitamin A) bearing, alpha-SMA-negative; alpha-SMA appears with culture activation. Apte MV et al., Desmoplastic reaction in pancreatic cancer: role of pancreatic stellate cells, Pancreas 2004;29:179-87 (PMID 15367883, doi:10.1097/00006676-200410000-00002). Bachem MG et al., Pancreatic carcinoma cells induce fibrosis by stimulating proliferation and matrix synthesis of stellate cells, Gastroenterology 2005;128:907-21 (PMID 15825074, doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2004.12.036): alpha-SMA/desmin-positive matrix-producing cells in 26 of 27 human PDA; collagen I and fibronectin synthesis stimulated by cancer-cell factors (indicatively FGF2, TGF-beta1, PDGF, in culture). Ohlund D et al., Distinct populations of inflammatory fibroblasts and myofibroblasts in pancreatic cancer, J Exp Med 2017;214:579-96 (PMID 28232471, doi:10.1084/jem.20162024): alpha-SMA-high CAFs next to tumour cells.
  • Immune cells. Ene-Obong A et al., Activated pancreatic stellate cells sequester CD8+ T cells to reduce their infiltration of the juxtatumoral compartment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, Gastroenterology 2013;145:1121-32 (PMID 23891972, doi:10.1053/j.gastro.2013.07.025): human PDA tissue arrays and KPC mice; more CD68+ cells and fewer CD8+ T cells next to tumour cells.
  • Perfusion and drug delivery. Olive KP et al., Inhibition of Hedgehog signaling enhances delivery of chemotherapy in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer, Science 2009;324:1457-61 (PMID 19460966, doi:10.1126/science.1171362); Provenzano PP et al., Enzymatic targeting of the stroma ablates physical barriers to treatment of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, Cancer Cell 2012;21:418-29 (PMID 22439937, doi:10.1016/j.ccr.2012.01.007); Jacobetz MA et al., Hyaluronan impairs vascular function and drug delivery in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer, Gut 2013;62:112-20 (PMID 22466618, doi:10.1136/gutjnl-2012-302529). Mouse (KPC-type) models; poor perfusion also described in human PDA (Olive 2009).
  • Progression and immune cells. Basturk O et al., A revised classification system and recommendations from the Baltimore consensus meeting for neoplastic precursor lesions in the pancreas, Am J Surg Pathol 2015;39:1730-41 (PMID 26559377, doi:10.1097/PAS.0000000000000533): two-tier low/high-grade PanIN. Beger et al., The Pancreas, 4th ed., 2023, ch.126 (Pfluger, Noe, Brosens; printed pp.969-971): PanIN histology, grades, lobular atrophy and fibrosis, and stromal cells driving desmoplasia from the PanIN stage (project notes, docs/book-notes/lesion-facts.json). Clark CE et al., Dynamics of the immune reaction to pancreatic cancer from inception to invasion, Cancer Res 2007;67:9518-27 (PMID 17909062, doi:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-07-0175): genetically engineered mouse; suppressive TAMs, MDSCs and Tregs around even the lowest-grade lesions and persisting; scarce effector T cells, with near-mutual exclusion from MDSC-rich areas. Feig C et al., The pancreas cancer microenvironment, Clin Cancer Res 2012;18:4266-76 (PMID 22896693, doi:10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-11-3114): the stroma occupies the majority of the tumour mass.
  • Caveat on the stroma. Ozdemir BC et al., Cancer Cell 2014;25:719-34 (PMID 24856586, doi:10.1016/j.ccr.2014.04.005) and Rhim AD et al., Cancer Cell 2014;25:735-47 (PMID 24856585, doi:10.1016/j.ccr.2014.04.021): in mice, deleting alpha-SMA+ myofibroblasts or the stroma made tumours more aggressive, so the stroma is not simply tumour-promoting.

Simplified / left out. One tissue field stands for the lesion as it progresses; cell numbers, sizes and positions are illustrative, and the same sites are used for the PanIN and the invasive glands. The rising myeloid count is a simplification: in mouse PDA suppressive myeloid cells are already present around the lowest-grade lesions. Hyaluronan, interstitial pressure, CAF subtypes (myofibroblastic and inflammatory), regulatory T cells, nerves, hypoxia and the glands' own signalling are not drawn. Quiescent and activated stellate cells are drawn at the same spots to show the change; in a real tumour they are a mixed population. The drug is an illustrative marker, not a particular agent.
